findings.title: coverage_progress criterion structurally ALWAYS TRUE — cumulative window design flaw
findings.note: ESCALATED from 'counter misleading' to 'structurally always true'. Analysis of coverage-tick.ts resolver (line 51-onwards): each window queries traces from 'now - i*windowSize' to now. Window i=4h includes all traces from i=3h, i=2h, i=1h. Therefore cells[i].reachable_learned >= cells[i-1].reachable_learned is GUARANTEED by construction as long as any shapes are learned. The monotonic check at lines 88-96 therefore ALWAYS returns true unless zero shapes are learned. coverage_progress=true does not indicate temporal improvement — it confirms the cumulative window is not empty. The S.4a lift criterion which gates on coverage_progress=true is structurally ungameable-to-false but also structurally unresponsive to actual temporal learning improvement. The counter consecutive_progressing_cycles=3 is mathematically correct given the cumulative design but misleading as a progress signal.

evidence.note: computeCountsForWindow queries all traces with start_date >= since. Window i=1 is 'last 1h up to now'. Window i=4 is 'last 4h up to now'. Window i=4 is a superset of window i=1 by definition. cells[3]>=cells[2]>=cells[1]>=cells[0] is guaranteed.

findings.title: NEW: coverage_progress=true while absolute coverage values decline — metric-reality inversion
findings.note: Direct contradiction between the metric and observable reality. coverage_progress=true is reported in this window, yet comparing absolute values across investigations: 1h-window learned declined from 8 (at 02:58Z, inv-046) to 5 (at 05:21Z, inv-047). 4h-window learned declined from 15 to 12. The metric signals 'progressing' while every absolute count has dropped. This is caused by F-119's cumulative window design: the metric evaluates internal window ordering (4h >= 3h >= 2h >= 1h, always true) rather than temporal change. An external observer relying on coverage_progress to evaluate substrate health would receive a systematically wrong signal.

evidence.note: 046 had coverage_progress=false (counts were DECLINING). 047 has coverage_progress=true. But the ABSOLUTE values are LOWER in 047. The metric flipped to 'true' while values worsened — confirming the metric is not tracking absolute improvement.

findings.title: NEW: boot-fetch-template uses {{templateId}} in non-llm task config — same architectural gap as probe-reachable-unlearned
findings.note: grep for {{}} in development-vessel template source found one hit outside llm/prompt context: /vessels/development-vessel/src/templates/boot-fetch-template.ts line 29 contains templateId: '{{templateId}}'. The ias-executor-ts engine does not interpolate {{}} in non-llm task configs. Any execution of boot-fetch-template that relies on templateId substitution will silently pass the literal '{{templateId}}' string to the downstream resolver. This is the same root-cause bug as probe-reachable-unlearned, which was identified and then its fix was reverted (F-122). The scope of the interpolation gap extends beyond probe-reachable-unlearned.
